title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook — Process, Runbooks, Postmortems, Rotations, Game Days, and Comms Templates
author: Ethan Chen
body:
Summary

This document is Redwood Inference’s canonical on-call and incident response playbook. It defines severity levels, detection and triage flows, runbook structure and examples, escalation matrices, rotation policy and handoff checklist, game day guidance, and templates for status page and customer communications. The goal is to keep services reliable, reduce time-to-recovery (MTTR), and ensure clear internal and external communications during incidents.

Scope

Applies to all public-facing Redwood runtime services and orchestration components (API gateway, inference runtime, model store, billing pipeline, telemetry and console). Internal infra incidents are covered where they materially affect customer-facing SLOs.

Key Responsibilities

- On-call Engineer (Primary): First responder for alerts; performs initial triage and mitigation steps from runbooks.
- Secondary / Follow-on: Provides technical backup, takes over paging when primary is overloaded.
- Incident Commander (IC): Coordinates cross-team response for Sev1/Sev2 incidents, owns incident lifecycle, internal comms cadence, and postmortem drive.
- Service Owner (Dev team): Technical ownership of mitigation and long-term fix.
- SRE Manager: Supports escalation to leadership, post-incident review, and SLO adjustments.
- Customer Success / Support: Customer-facing communications and escalation to affected accounts.

Channels and Tools

- PagerDuty: primary alerting; policies: api-gateway, runtime-availability, gpu-capacity, billing-errors.
- Slack channels: #oncall (private), #incidents (public summary channel), #postmortems (archival).
- Status Page: status.redwood.ai (public) with components and scheduled maintenance.
- Incident tracker: JIRA project INF-INC (all incidents tracked with a ticket).
- Runbooks: Confluence runbooks indexed below; ops-runbook repository for scripts.

Severity Definitions and SLOs

- Sev1 (Critical): Service unavailable or severe degradation impacting >20% of production requests or a major security/data incident. Target ack: 5m; Target mitigation (partial): 30m; IC required.
- Sev2 (High): Significant degradation affecting 5-20% of requests or single-region impact causing customer-visible errors. Target ack: 10m; Target mitigation: 2h.
- Sev3 (Medium): Reduced functionality or localized error rates <5% with no immediate customer impact. Target ack: 2h; Target mitigation: 24h.
- Sev4 (Low): Non-urgent issues, maintenance or minor backend errors. Target ack: 3 business days.

SLO examples (service-level):

- API Gateway: 99.95% availability (p95 latency <200ms for text-generation endpoints).
- Inference Runtime (hosted): 99.9% availability for served models; token-generation p99 latency per model profile tracked in model catalog.
- Embeddings API: 99.95% availability; p95 latency <100ms.

Incident lifecycle (high level)

1. Detection & Alerting
  - Automated alerts (metrics, error rates, budget breaches) route through PagerDuty.
  - Support/CS reports escalate via #oncall or on-call pager.
2. Triage (First 15 minutes)
  - Primary acknowledges alert, documents initial symptoms in JIRA INF-INC-<id>.
  - Collect: affected services, error messages, approximate impact, last deploys, recent config changes, relevant logs/traces.
3. Containment & Mitigation
  - Run immediate mitigations from runbooks (e.g., rollback, restart, route to fallback, scale up dedicated pool).
  - If mitigation fails or impact is broad, declare Incident and assign IC.
4. Incident Management (IC-led)
  - IC posts incident brief in #incidents and opens public status page incident.
  - Cadence: initial update at 15m (or on declaration), then every 30m until containment, then hourly.
5. Recovery & Verification
  - Confirm service health via synthetic checks and customer reports.
  - Close incident only after a sustained recovery window (default 15 minutes of green metrics unless otherwise specified).
6. Postmortem & Remediation
  - IC assigns postmortem owner (usually service owner). Full postmortem due within 7 business days; blameless root cause analysis and action items tracked with owners and deadlines.

Escalation matrix

- If Primary does not acknowledge within target ack: Pager escalates to Secondary.
- If Secondary does not resolve within mitigation target: Escalate to Service Owner and SRE Manager.
- For Sev1 incidents or security incidents: Notify VP Eng and Head of Security within 30 minutes.

On-call rotations and handoffs

- Rotation model: weekly primary on-call with a secondary on-call for the same week. Rotation is auto-managed by PagerDuty schedule.
- Coverage: primary (00:00 Mon local -> 23:59 Sun local); overlap handoff period is 15 minutes.
- Weekend policy: reduced staffing but same SLOs; secondary supports on-call phone.

Handoff checklist (to be completed in Slack thread and attach to JIRA INF-INC when handing over):

1. Confirm you have no active incidents and all alerts are acknowledged.
2. Share ongoing maintenance windows, deploys, or escalations planned for your shift.
3. Run health checks: API gateway synthetic, runtime pool utilization, queue backlogs, billing pipeline lag. Paste results.
4. Confirm calendar availability for the week and emergency contact number.

Runbook index and examples

Each runbook follows a standard template: Purpose, Scope, Detection (metrics/alerts), Quick Checks, Mitigation Steps (ordered), Rollback steps, Post-incident tasks, Owner and runbook last-updated.

1) API Gateway — High 5xx Rate (runbook id: RB-APIGW-01)

Purpose: Rapidly reduce customer errors when API gateway returns elevated 5xx rates.
Detection: Alert: api-gateway-5xx-rate > 1% for 3 minutes or error spike > 3x baseline.
Quick checks:
- Check recent deploys: kubectl get deploys --namespace apigw | grep -E "(api-gateway)" and review CI pipeline.
- Check ingress controller logs for error patterns and timeouts.
- Verify upstream target health in load balancer and service discovery.

Mitigation steps (ordered):
1. If a bad deploy is suspected, initiate rollback to previous stable tag (CI rollback command: ci rollback api-gateway --to stable).
2. If upstream targets failing, remove unhealthy instances from LB and scale up fallback pool: kubectl scale deployment api-gateway-fallback --replicas=3.
3. Enable temporary rate-limiting rule for non-authenticated endpoints (WAF toggle documented in infra runbooks).
4. If latency-induced 5xx, divert traffic to dedicated edge region using traffic-router: router switch --component apigw --target region-us-west-2.
5. Notify CS and update status page.

Rollback and recovery verification:
- After rollback/mitigation, run synthetic curl checks against /health and sample generation endpoints. Confirm p95 latency and error rate are within SLOs for 15 consecutive minutes.

2) Inference Runtime — Token-generation Latency Spike (RB-RUNTIME-02)

Purpose: Reduce high latency for token generation on hosted models.
Detection: runtime-latency-p95 > model-profile-threshold for >2m or queue depth > 80% of buffer.
Quick checks:
- Check GPU pool utilization (grafana panel: gpu-pool-util).
- Check model worker logs for OOMs or kernel errors.
- Review KV cache hit-rate metrics.

Mitigation steps:
1. If a model recent deploy occurred, temporarily pin requests to last stable model version in routing policy.
2. Increase autoscale target for the affected model pool by 20%: infra scale gpu-pool --pool <name> --scale +20.
3. Enable degraded-mode: reduce max sequence length and lower concurrency per worker to keep tail latency bounded (configuration flag: runtime.degraded_mode=true).
4. If root cause is memory pressure, restart affected workers in a rolling fashion with drain: infra restart worker --pool <name> --drain=true.

Verification: Confirm p95 and queue depths return to normal for 20 minutes. Document changed config in JIRA.

3) GPU Pool — Capacity Shortage (RB-GPU-03)

Purpose: Fast actions when reserved/dedicated pools cannot satisfy queued requests.
Detection: pending-jobs > threshold 500 or average wait-time > 30s for > 3m.
Quick checks:
- Confirm capacity events in cloud console, pending spot evictions, and autoscaler logs.
- Check capacity reservations for dedicated customers and overflow policies.

Mitigation steps:
1. Burst to secondary cloud region (if policy allows): infra route-traffic --from region-a --to region-b --component runtime.
2. Temporarily enable preemptible instance fallback for non-SLA traffic.
3. For dedicated pools, invoke emergency capacity allocation per contract and notify Account Executive and CS.
4. If sustained, trigger incident to engage capacity engineering for long-term fix.

Post-incident: Allocate cost ledger entries for emergency capacity and tag invoices accordingly.

Postmortem template and expectations

All Sev1 and Sev2 incidents require a blameless postmortem using the following template posted in /confluence/#postmortems and linked to the incident JIRA:

- Title: short descriptive title with date and incident id.
- Summary: one-paragraph incident summary and customer impact.
- Timeline: minute-by-minute timeline including detection, mitigation actions and state changes.
- Root cause: technical description and contributing factors.
- Detection & Response: what worked and what didn’t (alerts, runbooks, comms).
- Action items: clear remediation tasks with owners and due dates.
- Impact & Metrics: customers affected, error volume, duration, billing impact if any.
- Lessons learned and follow-ups.

Expectation: Postmortem draft due within 7 business days; final postmortem published and linked on status page incident within 14 business days. Action items tracked in the INF-ENG backlog and reviewed in weekly reliability sync until closed.

Game days and training

- Frequency: Quarterly game days coordinated by SRE and Platform teams; one tabletop and one live failover exercise per quarter.
- Objectives: validate runbooks, measure MTTA/MTTR, verify status page automations, test cross-team communications and customer comms cadence.
- Participants: SRE, runtime, infra, product, CS, and a rotating set of engineers from product teams.
- Scoring: measured on detection time, time-to-partial-mitigation, customer update quality, postmortem completeness.

Status page and customer communications templates

Public status page incident template (to post on status.redwood.ai):

- Title: [Incident] <Service> degraded — ongoing (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC)
- Impact: Brief summary of affected functionality and approximate percent of customers or requests impacted.
- Scope: Affected components / regions.
- Root cause (initial): Under investigation / brief initial hypothesis.
- Current status: Steps taken so far and immediate mitigation (e.g., traffic reroute, rollback).
- ETA: If known, otherwise: We will provide updates every 30 minutes until resolved.
- Next update: <time> UTC

Customer-facing email/comms template (for high-impact incidents)

Subject: Incident update — <short description> (Redwood Inference)

Hello <CustomerName>,

We are writing to let you know about an incident affecting <service/component>. Impact: <brief description — e.g., elevated error rates, increased latency, intermittent failures>.

What we know so far:
- Start time (UTC): <time>
- Affected services: <list>
- Scope of impact: <percent/customers/regions>

What we’re doing:
- Actions taken: <rollback, traffic routing, scaling>
- Next steps and ETA: <if known>

We will keep you updated via status.redwood.ai and directly through this thread. If you are experiencing a critical impact to your production workload, please reply to this message or contact your Account Team.

Apologies for the disruption.

Regards,
The Redwood Inference Operations team

Internal incident comms (Slack short-form)

/incident declare <INF-INC-1234> Sev1: API Gateway 5xx spike — IC @Marco, Primary @Ethan. Initial mitigation: rollback in progress. See JIRA INF-INC-1234 for details and timeline.

Post-incident follow-up and SLAs with customers

- For incidents with billing impact or SLA credit triggers, the finance and legal playbook is invoked. Account managers will coordinate credits and formal communications.
- SRE will propose SLA adjustments if recurring incidents exceed error budgets.

Operational metrics and dashboards to monitor

- Incident dashboard: open incidents by severity, MTTA, MTTR, postmortem age.
- Service health: p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, queue depth for runtime pools, GPU utilization, model load times.
- Alert noise metrics: false positive rate and alert-to-incident conversion.

Maintenance windows and planned changes

- All planned maintenance must be announced at least 72 hours in advance on the status page and in #incidents. For breaking changes, coordinate with SRE and CS at least 5 business days prior.
